91:1: His saying: And the sun and its brightness is an oath in which our Lord, may He be exalted, swears by the sun and its brightness. The meaning of the words is: He swears by the sun and by the brightness of the sun. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement, its morning. Some of them said: It means: the sun and the day. He used to say: the morning is the entire day. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the sun and its brightness. He said: This day. Others said: The meaning of this is: her ablution. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the sun and its brightness, he said: Its light. The correct thing to say about this is: God Almighty swore by the sun and its day, because the light of the visible sun is the day.
91:2: And His statement: And the moon when it follows it, God Almighty says: And the moon when it follows the sun, and that is in the first half of the month, when the sun sets, the moon follows it by rising. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the moon when it follows it, he said: It follows the day. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: And the moon when it follows it means: the sun when the moon covers it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the moon when it follows it, he said: follows it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the moon when it follows it. It follows it on the morning of the crescent, and when the sun sets, the crescent is seen. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the moon when it follows it, he said: When it follows it on the night of the crescent. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And the sun and its brightness, and the moon when it follows it, he said: This is a division, and the moon follows the sun during the first half of the month, and it follows it in the other half. As for the first half, it follows it, and its mother is behind it, and when it is the other half, it is in front of it, putting it forward, and it follows it.
91:3: And his saying: And the day when it reveals it, he says: And the day when it reveals it, he said: When it shines. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the day when it reveals it, he said: When the day covers it. Some of the Arabists interpreted this to mean: And the day when it reveals the darkness, and they made the ha’ and the alif from jalaha a metaphor for the darkness, and they said: It is permissible to use it as a metaphor, and it was not mentioned before, because its meaning is well-known, just as the meaning of the saying of the one who says: It became cold in the morning, and it went cold in the evening, and it blew from the north is well-known. So he used a metaphor for feminine nouns that were not mentioned when their meaning was well-known. What is correct in our view regarding this matter is what the scholars whose words we have mentioned said, because they are more knowledgeable about that, even though what the Arabists we mentioned said has a basis.
91:4: And His statement: And the night when it covers it means that God Almighty says: And the night when it covers the sun until it sets and the horizons become dark. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saad told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the night when it covers it: when the night covers it.
91:5: And His statement: And the heaven and He who constructed it, God Almighty says: And He who constructed it, meaning: And He who created it, and His construction of it: His making it a roof for the earth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the heaven and He who constructed it. And its construction means its creation. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the heaven and He who constructed it, he said: God constructed the heaven. It was said, And what built it, and He, the Most High, is its Builder. He placed what in place of whom, just as He said, And a father and what he begot (al-Balad 90:3). He placed what in place of whom and its meaning, and whom he begot, because it is an oath swore by Adam and his son. Likewise, And do not marry those women your fathers married (An-Nisa’: 22). And His statement, Then marry those that please you (An-Nisa’: 3). Rather, it is: Then marry those that please you. It is permissible to direct that to the meaning of the source, as if he said: the sky and its construction, and a father and his birth.
